_comment: Single source of truth for workflow SHAPE (the second axis). The task-type registry says what each node SAYS (routing + workflow prose); THIS registry says the node SEQUENCE — which agents a workflow runs, in what order, its verify policy, its stop condition, AND which checkpoint verifiers it fans out. The shape is PARTIALLY LOAD-BEARING: the `verifiers` field drives the checkpoint fan-out (dispatch.py cmd_dispatch_next + _step_emit_dispatch_batch iterate verifiers_for(shape)), so a project shape omitting test-runner simply doesn't fan it out. The `nodes` topology STAYS ADVISORY: shape_allows (dispatch.py) consults it only to attach a `shape_violation` disclosure when an action's agent is off-topology — never to block or reroute — and the planner→executor→checker spine runs unchanged regardless of the resolved shape. (nodes is the SPINE topology; verifiers are its checkpoint CHILDREN — distinct lists, never conflated: a phase-checker dispatching a verifier is on-topology even though the verifier is not in nodes.) The other accessors (verify_policy_for / stop_condition_for / instruction_for / planning_doc_for) feed `registry-doc --shape` display and the PLANNING layer ONLY — none is injected into a dispatch prompt (contrast the task-type `workflow` field, which IS). `research-first`'s explore-before-plan intent is honored at the PLANNING layer via its planning docfile's Prelude (explorer dispatched before spec-planner); the dispatch spine itself never reorders — an off-topology dispatch still surfaces a `shape_violation` disclosure. (A project may still overlay conductor/workflow/workflow-shapes.json — opt-in by file presence — to add or override shapes with zero plugin edits; the rows resolve, render, and — for the verifier axis — drive the fan-out.)

_fields.nodes: the ordered list of SPINE dispatch agents this shape runs (the topology). Action tokens: spec-planner | explorer | task-executor | phase-checker. ADVISORY: shape_allows consults this only to surface a `shape_violation` disclosure when an off-topology agent dispatches — it does NOT block. Checkpoint verifiers (ac-tracer / build-runner / test-runner) are NOT spine nodes; they are checkpoint children declared in `verifiers` below, and a phase-checker dispatching one is on-topology regardless of `nodes`.
_fields.verifiers: the ordered verifier-agent list fanned out at this shape's checkpoint (checkpoint CHILDREN of the spine — distinct from `nodes`, the spine topology). Each entry must be a verifier name (`ac-tracer` | `build-runner` | `test-runner`). The fan-out emits one wave member per entry (the per-member envelope built inline by `_build_verifier`); the three fan out IN PARALLEL as a cheapest-first graduated gate — `build-runner` (L0 compile/typecheck floor, fail-fast on uncompilable code) → `test-runner` (L1 suite) → `ac-tracer` (AC evidence), synthesized by `phase-checker`. Absent/empty => the standard [ac-tracer, build-runner, test-runner] triple (fail-open). Unknown entries are dropped at fan-out. This is the load-bearing seam that makes a shape control WHICH verifiers its checkpoint runs. A test-grounded shape (ac_grounding != review) MUST include build-runner — dropping the build tier reopens the 'unimported module' hole (code the suite never imports); only a review-grounded shape (`deliverable`) may omit it (the review attestation is its substitute).
_fields.requires: optional prerequisites the shape demands of track-state before it can run (advisory; future hook). Absent => no prerequisites.
_fields.verify_policy: how this shape gates progress: checkpoint (the default — phase-checker stamps a checkpoint gate) | none (no checkpoint gate — research/exploration shapes that produce no committable artifact).
_fields.stop_condition: what makes the shape DONE: all_nodes_done (every node in `nodes` has run) | a structured pass_condition. The fixed spine's default is all_nodes_done.
_fields.gates: the quality gates this shape enforces at the TRACK level — the ON/OFF each gate composes with the per-task exemption (a gate fires for a task iff (gate in gates) AND (not task_exempt)). Members: tdd (F2 red/green/refactor) | coverage (F3 >=80%) | checkpoint (F5 — the phase-checker checkpoint GATES progress; distinct from verify_policy, which is whether a checkpoint phase runs AT ALL). Absent/empty => the default shape's gates => the full set (today's behavior). The seam that lets a non-code shape drop F2/F3 at the track level while keeping the checkpoint.
_fields.ac_grounding: how acceptance criteria are GROUNDED for this shape. test (default) => ACs are grounded by test_TC_* functions (the basis of spec_integrity's grounding scan). review => ACs are grounded by an artifact anchor + a review attestation (a non-code deliverable shape — docs, design, research, a data deliverable), so the grounding scan reads anchors/attestations instead of test functions. A shape whose ACs ground another way declares it here so the grounding scan does not insist on test-grounding a non-test shape. Absent => test.
_fields.checkpoint_policy: whether this shape's checkpoint phase actually RUNS. run (default) => the phase-checker checkpoint fans out as normal (every shipped shape). skip-if-declared => short-circuit the checkpoint emit, but ONLY when the shape declares an integrity substitute (ac_grounding=review => the review attestation is the substitute); a skip-if-declared shape with NO declared substitute FAILS HARD (a shape_violation halt), never a silent skip. This is the 3rd load-bearing drives-dispatch field (after verifiers + gates); absent => run (today's behavior). The 'attach a guarantee to every freedom' invariant: checkpoint_policy must not become a second advisory nodes.
_fields.instruction: optional inline planning prose for the shape (mirrors the task-type `workflow` field). The LEGACY small form — the preferred home for a shape's planning procedure is a planning-library docfile named by `planning_doc` (below); a row carrying BOTH holds the procedure in two homes and is rejected by the strict-write validator. No shipped shape carries `instruction` anymore.
_fields.planning_doc: the planning-library docfile carrying this shape's PLANNING PROCEDURE (`templates/planning/<name>.md` plugin side, `conductor/planning/<name>.md` project side — project wins), named as a bare `.md` filename. The docfile has two audiences: an orchestrator-facing Prelude (pre-planning steps new-track runs BEFORE dispatching spec-planner — e.g. research-first's explorer dispatch) and a planner-facing body (shape-specific spec/plan authoring guidance). Docfiles carry PROCEDURE only — signals, gates, verifiers, grounding stay registry-owned fields. A project adds a custom planning workflow = one docfile + one shape row, zero plugin edits. Absent => inherit the default shape's `planning_doc`.
_fields.signals: the keyword list `track-state propose-shape` matches against the track description ⊕ brief to rank this shape as a candidate (mirrors task-type `signals` / derive_task_tag: lowercase keywords, multi-word phrases allowed, substring-matched). Only shapes that declare `signals` are candidates; the `default` shape deliberately omits it — it is the fail-open fallback when no candidate clears the bar, never a competitor. Absent => not a propose-shape candidate.
_fields.max_retries: the shape-level default retry budget for tasks under this shape: an int >= 1 (0/absent => inherit the global MAX_RETRIES). The chain is task.max_retries > this > global (constants.task_max_retries resolves it; every enforcement site reads through that resolver). Use when a job family needs a different ceiling than the default 3 — e.g. a migration shape may declare 1 (each retry re-runs a risky port), a research shape may declare more (dead ends are the job).

research-first.when_to_use: A research-heavy track — one whose first need is UNDERSTANDING (map the codebase / survey a dependency / spike an approach) before planning. Explore-before-plan is honored at the PLANNING layer: this shape's planning docfile Prelude has the orchestrator dispatch explorer BEFORE spec-planner and pass the Exploration Notes forward as planning input. The dispatch spine itself still never reorders (`nodes` stays advisory — an off-topology dispatch surfaces a `shape_violation` disclosure), and the executor tasks afterward run the full inherited gates.

migration.when_to_use: A behavior-PRESERVATION track — migrating code (framework upgrade, API rename, refactor across module boundaries) where correctness is witnessed by the EXISTING test suite, not new tests. The shape drops the tdd/coverage gates at the track level (gates=[checkpoint]): tasks owe a green existing suite at the checkpoint, not new tests or >=80% coverage. Pair with the [Migrate] task-type tag, whose `workflow` prose the executor fetches instead of TDD — the tag carries the executor guidance, the shape carries the gate paradigm (the conductor's two-registry separation: task-types own node behavior, shapes own topology + gates).

deliverable.when_to_use: A non-code DELIVERABLE track — producing an artifact that is NOT a tested code change (a design doc, a research report, a spec, a runbook, a data deliverable) where correctness is witnessed by an artifact anchor + a review attestation, not by automated tests. The shape drops the test-runner verifier (no tests to run — ac-tracer alone fans out at the checkpoint) and grounds ACs by review (ac_grounding=review), so each AC maps to a concrete deliverable anchor a reviewer attests rather than a test_TC_* function. Pair with a task-type tag whose `workflow` prose carries the executor guidance for producing the deliverable (the conductor's two-registry separation: task-types own node behavior, shapes own topology + grounding) — the tag carries the executor prose, the shape carries the verifier set + the grounding paradigm.
